clue.text: Extra short box

indicators.note: something short is lacking its end, so the last letter is cut off

blocks.note: a spare is an extra one kept in reserve

explanation.surface: A request for a little extra box, perhaps a smaller carton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' looks like a container noun, but it is the verb: to spar is to box in practice.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to fight with fists in training, a synonym of the verb box.

clue.text: Barmy old crook in part of Italy

indicators.note: as a verb, crook means to bend out of shape, so the letters are twisted

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mad elderly criminal is hiding out somewhere in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crook' reads as a noun for a villain; here it is a verb meaning bend. Barmy is British slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Lombardy is a northern region of Italy whose capital is Milan.

clue.text: Extremely mean falsehoods stopping Mr T moving south

indicators.note: in a down entry south is the bottom, so one letter of the title travels to the end
to stop a gap is to plug it, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: Mr is short for mister; its letter T is the one that moves
falsehoods are untruths

explanation.surface: Someone stingy is telling lies to halt the celebrity Mr T as he heads south.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, south means the bottom, so the T of the title drops to the end and the falsehoods fill the space just above it.
explanation.definitionFit: Miserliest is the superlative of miserly, so it means most stingy, the extreme of mean.

clue.text: You and I run, revealing fungal problem

blocks.note: the pronoun for you and me together
a trot is a gentle run

explanation.surface: Two people go running and discover their house has a fungal problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Wet rot is a fungus that decays damp timber, a household problem of the fungal kind.

clue.text: Insert ad to shift items for part exchange?

indicators.note: shifting things moves them around, so these letters change their order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dealer places a newspaper advert to sell off goods taken as part exchange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shift' reads as selling stock, which fits the advert; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade-in is an old item handed over as partial payment towards a new purchase.

clue.text: Cockney tramp heard musical instrument

indicators.note: heard means we go by how the word is spoken rather than spelt

blocks.note: a tramp is a hobo, and a Cockney drops the initial H

explanation.surface: A vagrant from East London is heard playing a woodwind.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the London accent famous for dropping the H at the start of words.
explanation.definitionFit: The oboe is a double-reed woodwind instrument, an example of a musical instrument.

clue.text: Component of sandstone church (but not the northern quarter)

indicators.note: in a down entry north is the top, and a quarter of eight letters is two, so the top two go

blocks.note: a basilica is a large church

explanation.surface: Part of a sandstone church, apart from its northern section.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sandstone church' reads as one phrase; the definition stops at sandstone.
explanation.definitionFit: Silica, silicon dioxide, is the quartz mineral that makes up most of the grains in sandstone.

clue.text: One third of American state is cut off, unfortunately

indicators.note: a third of a six-letter name is two letters, and that share is what gets removed
cutting off a part removes it, here from the end of the state's name

blocks.note: the largest US state

explanation.surface: Sadly, a third of a US state has been isolated from the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: Alaska really is cut off from the other mainland states, which hides the deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas is an exclamation of regret, used just as one would say unfortunately.

clue.text: Staff nearly able to charge Michelle Mone, perhaps - an amoral businesswoman

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the final letter is left off
to charge a gun is to load it, so these letters are packed inside

blocks.note: a rod is a staff or stick
fit as in capable, fit to do something
she sits in the House of Lords as a baroness

explanation.surface: Accusing the Conservative baroness of being a ruthless businesswoman.
explanation.walkthrough: Michelle Mone is a British businesswoman and Tory peer criticised over pandemic protective-equipment contracts; she does double duty in the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A profiteer makes excessive gains from others' need, typically in a crisis, which marks someone as an unscrupulous trader.

clue.text: Fantastic swimmer

blocks.note: first meaning: British slang short for brilliant
second meaning: a European flatfish

explanation.surface: Praise for an excellent swimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' suggests a person in a pool; crosswords often use it for a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both chatty British slang for excellent and the name of a flatfish related to turbot.

clue.text: Jewish leader, one declining to reflect?

indicators.note: a reflection shows things mirrored, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: to ebb is to decline, so one who declines is an ebber

explanation.surface: A rabbi who refuses to stop and think about things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Declining' sounds like refusing; it is the sense of waning, as a tide ebbs.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebbe is a Hasidic rabbi, the spiritual head of a Jewish community.

clue.text: Director delivers plays for parachutists

indicators.note: to play with something is to fiddle about with it, so these letters get rearranged

blocks.note: D is a standard abbreviation for director
taken as written

explanation.surface: A theatre director produces dramas aimed at skydivers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plays' looks like theatre after 'Director'; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Devils are the British Army's Parachute Regiment display team, famous parachutists.

clue.text: My son hired out body armour

blocks.note: both are exclamations of surprise
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
to let a property is to rent it out

explanation.surface: A parent explains that their son rented out some armour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks like a possessive; it is the exclamation, as in 'My!' Cor is the British equivalent.
explanation.definitionFit: A corslet is a piece of armour covering the torso, a breastplate.

clue.text: Philosopher quietly leaves University grounds

indicators.note: whatever leaves a place is no longer there, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: p, piano, is the musical marking for soft
a campus is the grounds of a university

explanation.surface: A thinker slips away from the campus without a sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Camus was a French author and existentialist thinker, an example of a philosopher.

clue.text: Break actually overwhelms rector

indicators.note: to overwhelm is to engulf, so one piece swallows the other

blocks.note: in fact means actually
R is an abbreviation for rector

explanation.surface: A clergyman is overpowered by an interruption, as it happens.
explanation.definitionFit: To infract is to violate a rule or law, so it means break in that legal sense.

clue.text: Unrestricted racer Terry feels odd

indicators.note: something odd is out of the ordinary, so these letters are put in an unusual order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A competitor named Terry, freed from rules, feels a bit strange.
explanation.definitionFit: A freestyler competes in freestyle events, where the stroke or technique is not restricted.

clue.text: Sex up left-winger, getting exhausted

indicators.note: in a down entry going up means the word is read from the bottom

blocks.note: it is a coy word for sex
a red is a socialist or communist

explanation.surface: Adding spice to a socialist's image leaves them worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sex up' reads as the phrase for making something racier; it splits into sex and the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tired and exhausted are synonyms, both describing someone drained of energy.

clue.text: Article by American lying about crowds, perhaps

indicators.note: a crowd hems people in, so the clue words enclose the letters wanted
lying about means turned around, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the end of the first word, the middle word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A news piece written by an untruthful American draws large audiences, possibly.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'articlE BY AMerican' and are read right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: Maybe and perhaps are adverbs of possibility, each one a straightforward synonym of the other.

clue.text: Naughtinesses cryptically resulting in plea for help

indicators.note: cryptically tells us to split the word into parts and read it as a recipe

blocks.note: read as naught in esses: a zero placed inside two letters S

explanation.surface: Bad behaviour ends with a cry for rescue.
explanation.walkthrough: Naught means nought, the figure 0, and esses are letters S; nought in esses puts O between two S's.
explanation.definitionFit: SOS is the international distress signal, the classic call for help.

clue.text: Settled matter in court, at last, after side upset team members

indicators.note: to upset something is to knock it over, so these letters are thrown into a new order
at last points to the final letter of the word before it
after places one piece behind the other in the answer

blocks.note: taken as written, before being knocked out of order
the players in a team are its men
the final letter of court

explanation.surface: A legal dispute was settled after one side unsettled the opposing players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settled matter in court' reads as a lawsuit; the definition is just 'Settled matter', with 'in' a link to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Sediment is material that settles to the bottom of a liquid, literally matter that has settled.

clue.text: Senior metalworker wanting wife

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so that letter is missing

blocks.note: a welder joins metal
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: An older tradesman who would like to get married.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanting wife' reads as longing for a spouse; it means without W.
explanation.definitionFit: An elder is a senior person, especially an older member of a community or church.

clue.text: Young socialite, before playing field, went naked in Hungarian city

indicators.note: before puts the first piece ahead of the next in the answer
naked means stripped of its covering, so the outer letters go and the middle stays

blocks.note: a deb, debutante, is a young woman entering society
the rec, recreation ground, is a British public playing field
went with its first and last letters stripped

explanation.surface: A debutante streaked across a sports ground somewhere in Hungary.
explanation.definitionFit: Debrecen is the second-largest city in Hungary, in the east of the country.

clue.text: Extremely safe saw is made quieter

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, the first and last letters

blocks.note: the first and last letters of safe
to see someone is to go out with them, so saw means dated

explanation.surface: A very secure saw has been silenced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the tool; it is the past of see in the romantic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedated means calmed with a drug, so a patient who is sedated has been made quieter.

clue.text: Surprising delivery from saint bearing a cross returned

indicators.note: the saint and the cross are carried together, one held inside the other
something returned goes back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
a rood is a crucifix
S is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A saint carrying a cross comes back to deliver an unexpected parcel.
explanation.walkthrough: The saint goes inside A ROOD and the whole is reversed. 'Delivery' is the cricket sense, a ball bowled.
explanation.definitionFit: A doosra is an off-spinner's ball that turns the opposite way from usual, a cricket ball meant to deceive the batter.

clue.text: Spooner's favourite cuddly toy that is used for experiments

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so we do the same here

blocks.note: the favourite is the best, and a cuddly toy is a ted, short for teddy

explanation.surface: A child's best-loved teddy bear ends up as a lab subject.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the B and T of BEST TED.
explanation.definitionFit: A testbed is a platform or setting where new equipment or ideas are trialled, so it is used for experiments.

clue.text: Sluggish hill descent coming up

indicators.note: in a down entry coming up means rising from the bottom, so the word reads backwards

blocks.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor
a dip is a downward slope

explanation.surface: A slow walker finds a downhill stretch turning into a climb.
explanation.definitionFit: Torpid means inactive and lethargic, a close synonym of sluggish.

clue.text: Later on, I'm performing circus act

definitions.note: the answer is the performer rather than the act

indicators.note: performing means putting on a show, so these letters act out a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A performer announces that their circus turn comes later in the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Performing' fits the circus picture; it is also the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A lion-tamer is the star of a big-cat routine under the big top, a classic circus turn.

clue.text: Girl left behind in America

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
ass is US slang for the backside

explanation.surface: A young woman was left behind when the others went to the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left behind' reads as one phrase; split it, and behind is the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Lass is a mainly Scottish and northern English word for a girl or young woman.

clue.text: Drag queen's bottom seen in Eccles?

indicators.note: in a down entry the bottom of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: to tow is to drag along
the last letter of queen

explanation.surface: A drag queen's backside on view in the setter's namesake town.
explanation.walkthrough: Eccles is the setter's own pseudonym as well as a place; the question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Eccles is a town near Manchester in north-west England, so it is one example of a town.

clue.text: Give and take

blocks.note: first meaning: to give way or surrender
second meaning: a noun for the return or takings produced

explanation.walkthrough: 'Give and take' is a familiar phrase for compromise; split it into two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield is to give in or give way, and as a noun a yield is the return or amount taken.

clue.text: Record short dance

indicators.note: short means cut down, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: a disco is a dance party

explanation.surface: A recording of a brief dance tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc is a gramophone record or CD, so it names a record.

clue.text: Prison officer bragged after start of sentence

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the opening letter of sentence
crew is an old past tense of crow, to brag

explanation.surface: A jail warder boasted once a prisoner's sentence began.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sentence' fits the prison picture, but only its first letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Screw is British prison slang for a jailer or warder.

clue.text: Running back is claiming tennis champion is silent

indicators.note: back means read in the opposite direction
to claim something is to take hold of it, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: a machine that is running is on
taken as written
Monica Seles won nine Grand Slam singles titles

explanation.surface: A tennis champion running back to the baseline stays quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Noiseless means making no sound at all, a synonym of silent.
